chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: @Benno Overeinder I asked Evan to present the RRSIG Refused

chat.author: Benno Overeinder
chat.text: Thanks Ondrej.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: But I will be here to answer any questions. But I thought it would be easier for people if Evan was presenting.

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: here's a pre-question: is there a reason not to include NSEC and NSEC3 in the QTYPEs that should be refused as your draft suggests?

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: Joe, pls bring to the mic if you'd like to ask the wG

chat.author: Christian Elmerot
chat.text: This is essentially only formalizing existing behaviour in some implementations

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: If you store signatures with the records, then it is non-trivial to lookup RRSIG.

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: nsec3 is already forbidden as a QTYPE

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: Ben is asking that question

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: RFC 8906 already allows NOTIMP for "meta RRs", but the jury is still out on whether ANY (see next preso) qualifies.

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: related note: that one domain of mine gets roughly 6 q/s for CNAME.  sigh.

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: NOTIMP is what knot resolver and 1.1.1.1 do, FWTW

chat.author: John Kristoff
chat.text: to geoff's point, could nodata work?

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: RFC 8482 section 4.1 allows a NODATA response I think

chat.author: Geoff Huston
chat.text: NODATA  has very little query duplication - its an efficient RCODE in today's DNS

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: John, I think that would require a proof of non-existence for the RRSIG type, which contradicts that RRSIG needs to appear in the NSEC type bitmap (which implies that it is not being proven non-existent)

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: the draft was written independently of ralf's slides; the draft proposes a continuation along the path of deprecating ANY altogether, but in a conservative way to avoid breaking things too badly

chat.author: Wes Hardaker
chat.text: lated note: that same small server of mine for the same domain of mine gets roughly 14 q/s for ANY. sigh.

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: for the record I agree with Ralf all the time!

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: Ondrej, for the intermediate Merge Request: interesting. Should require TCP for cache snooping, else return TC

chat.author: Shane Kerr
chat.text: Yeah. TCP seems reasonable.

chat.author: Joe Abley
chat.text: to be honest I would not be sad if cache snooping became more expensive

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: at the moment I TC ANY over UDP... I should see how many come back over TCP maybe

chat.author: Benjamin Schwartz
chat.text: Yeah, ANY for TCP=1 && RD=0 only seems like a good solution to me

chat.author: Christian Elmerot
chat.text: Responding to ANY with NOTIMP, FORMERR or HINFO should at least not be considered as a signal that the name exists ... sigh

chat.author: Ted Lemon
chat.text: Star Trek reference greatly appreciated, @Ralf

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: @Ondrej didn't we recently see issues with NODATA and ANY?

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: I appreciate ondrej's willingness to be incrementalist on this.

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text:
Should require TCP for cache snooping, else return TC

I like that...

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: (I've been the annoying person arguing to him that we shouldn't just kill it)

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text:
didn't we recently see issues with NODATA and ANY?

Yes, you can't do NODATA for ANY that's ENT

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: To rephrase this – as a resolver, you have no way how to distinguish NODATA response for the Empty Non-Terminal and NODATA response for a resolver that "kills ANY"

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: NODATA for ANY sounds dangerous given aggressive negative caching resolvers that do type inference.

chat.author: Roy Arends
chat.text: were the problems in 2015 and 2026 experienced by the same operator?

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text:
NODATA for ANY sounds dangerous given aggressive negative caching resolvers that do type inference.

Yes, that would not work with BIND 9. I considered the option, but you can't do that – not even from the resolver because the downstream resolver could cache this as NODATA(ANY) (ENT)

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Agreed Ondrej

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: Unfortunately, it would have been such an elegant solution...

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: here's a stupid idea.  NXRRSET?

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: semantically appropriate, except that it's only used by UPDATE, and not QUERY

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: yeah, that's why I called it stupid.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
chat.text: domain-set sounds like a great way to determine _all_ of the domains to attack if you want to cause the most mischief to a given entity with a DoS etc...

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: every now and again one of my stupid ideas does turn out to be useful, but I don't think this is one of those times

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: I wonder if the speaker has been referred to the DBOUND WG, which worked on this for a few years and folded without (IIRC) producing anythingl

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text:
NXRRSet -- RR Set that should exist does not

Not sure if this matches the intend usage

chat.author: Benno Overeinder
chat.text: I know (indirectly) this has been mentioned.  This is more focused.

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Yeah, he's aware of DBOUND and mentions it in the draft.

chat.author: Tim Wicinski
chat.text: yea I chatted with Tom about DBOUND etc with his initial draft

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: There was a thread on dnsop about this draft recently where the dbound history was rehashed.

chat.author: Tom Hill
chat.text: @Karl: I'm not sure the lessening of effort to determine an org's disparate use of domains cause DDoS attacks that cause greater harm - the harm is in the volume of queries, rather than what they're querying.

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: I couldn't find those mentions in his draft, but good that he's aware of them.

chat.author: Tom Hill
chat.text: Also the overhead of doing a recce on an org for a concerted attack, is par for the course; mail ops (et al.) as listed don't have the luxury of time.

chat.author: Karl Dyson
Evan Hunt
chat.text: I looked at the domain-set draft, skimmed the abstract, skipped immediately to "security considerations" and goggled a bit at the length of it.  feels like the risk to benefit ratio isn't that great

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: There's an icky bootstrapping issue. If l lookup foo.$TLD, where do I go to find out which domain name tells me which entity is responsible for foo.$TLD?

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: There's also staleness issue – this feels like the same problem that we already have with DNS with someone forgetting to update the delegation, that domain expires and miscreant registers it and redirects all your traffic.

chat.author: Barbara Bellis
chat.text: @jim reid - RDAP?

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: You are a bad lady Barbara. Very bad. :-)

chat.author: David Lawrence
chat.text: I would then provide pushback to the point that "DNSSEC is not widely deployed" that "Well this then provides more motivation to do so."

chat.author: Evan Hunt
chat.text: "why does proctor and gamble need 170 domain names in the first place? what's wrong with just registering pg.com and leaving it at that?" - a very young and naïve me

chat.author: David Lawrence
chat.text: See also: sony.com.

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: Not clear who the clients for this are other than Tom's registry

chat.author: David Lawrence
chat.text: (or, I am chagrined to say, Salesforce)

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: We had similar problems in DBOUND, could never agree what the question was

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text: +1 to Paul (on if this goes anywhere to a trust-related new WG)

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: why does shell.com need 6 kilobytes of TXT?

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Because mit.edu told them?

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: they tried to do more of what cloudflare.com does

chat.author: Shumon Huque
chat.text: Just publish https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-dnsop-domain-verification-techniques/ as an RFC and point shell (and MIT) to it. Particularly Appendix A.1

chat.author: Paul Wouters
chat.text: CLASS intranet ?    Runs away fast

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: I would think you would want a feature (e.g., when you switch to a VPN) which blows away things even if the other side said "trust me".

chat.author: Thomas Barrett
chat.text: re: domain-set.  Thanks for the comments.  More are welcomed on the list.  Ping me if you would like to discuss implementing or consuming.

chat.author: John Kristoff
chat.text: could this https global option be used against clients, i.e. tracking?

chat.author: John Levine
chat.text: @shumon stanford.edu even more so

chat.author: Erik Nygren
chat.text:
Re: globally-reachable.
DNSOP is the right place.  There are a bunch of sharp edges that I am not sure are solvable which I will send mail to the list about, but they are all things that would need to be worked through in DNSOP.

chat.text: Thank you Erik -- will look for the email, and agreed that it's going to need to be very carefully structured to thread the needle between a bunch of different issues, so hoping for expertise from folks in dnsop to help steer us away from some of the sharp edges :)

chat.text: @shumon I think the winner still if cisco.com: ;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 6947

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: DKIM doesn't need a a verifiable key, does it?

chat.author: Ondřej Surý
chat.text: And we worry about large DNSSEC signatures...

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: Just wait until those txt records get PQC signed

chat.author: Pete Resnick
chat.text: Maybe's it's needed for other things, but for DKIM, I don't think you need an issuer. Self-signed I think is fine.

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: @jim but it'll be one RRSIG(set) across the entire TXT RRset...

chat.author: Philip Homburg
chat.text: gzip and they will get smaller

chat.author: Peter Thomassen
chat.text: Jesus!

chat.author: Jim Reid
chat.text: True Ray, but just how big will that PQC signature be?

chat.author: Christian Elmerot
chat.text: Signature size is the same as for a single record

chat.author: Ray Bellis
chat.text: same as for any RRset, I think?

chat.text: isn't zstd faster and better than DEFLATE now?

chat.text: Thanks all :)
